blockMcqs.question: A hash map is called O(1). What does that actually guarantee?
options: Guaranteed O(1) for every operation, always
Average O(1); worst case is O(n)
O(log n) average, O(n) worst
O(1) only once the table is full
blockMcqs.explanation: Hashing is average-case constant time; collisions can pile up to O(n).

blockMcqs.question: What does a hash function return?
options: The final array index directly
An integer you fold into the table size
A sorted position for the key
A boolean: present or absent
blockMcqs.explanation: It yields an integer; `% slots` picks the slot, so resizing relocates keys.

blockMcqs.question: In open addressing, why can't you delete by just clearing the slot?
options: It would double the load factor
Clearing a slot is an O(n) operation
It breaks the probe chain to later keys
The hash function forbids empty slots
blockMcqs.explanation: A cleared slot cuts the probe chain, so you mark a tombstone instead.

blockMcqs.question: Why does resizing force every key to be rehashed?
options: The hash function itself changes
Keys are stored sorted and must reorder
The slot is hash % size, and size changed
To reset all the tombstones
blockMcqs.explanation: The index depends on table size, so a bigger table moves keys.

blockMcqs.question: Two Sum solved with a hash map runs in:
options: O(n²) time, O(1) space
O(n log n) time, O(1) space
O(n) time, O(n) space
O(log n) time, O(n) space
blockMcqs.explanation: One pass with O(1) complement lookups, storing up to n entries.

blockMcqs.question: When is a hash table the wrong choice?
options: Counting word frequencies
Membership tests
Range queries and sorted iteration
Exact-key lookup
blockMcqs.explanation: Hashing scatters keys, so ordered and range queries need a tree.

blockMcqs.question: How do you defend a public API against hash flooding?
options: Lower the load factor to zero
Use a seeded or randomized hash function
Disable resizing entirely
Replace the map with a set
blockMcqs.explanation: A per-process seed makes colliding keys unpredictable to attackers.
